sales_evidence.proven_price_band: $40-80 holds the volume (50 listings, 16,300+ units/mo; median ~$66-70) and $80-130 is proven (20 listings, 11,800+ units/mo, mostly oneisall at $84.99-$109.99 and Neakasa $82.99). $130+ is thin on Amazon (6 listings, ~200 units/mo) but DTC brands (FurMe $159.99, Uproot $179.99-$199.99) sell there with social ads. Our proven-band pick: $119 kit (inside $80-130). Economics only pass at about $179, which is outside the Amazon-proven band.

hero_spec.description: Corded 120V canister grooming vacuum, 2-2.5 L dust cup, 3 suction levels (12,000-15,000 Pa class, matching Buenkee/oneisall LM2-class units), hose with quick-connect; clipper head that runs on the vacuum hose (hair is sucked away as it is cut); deshedding blade, slicker brush, cleaning nozzle, 4-6 guide combs.
premium_vs_amazon_measurable: Safety: ETL or UL listed to UL 1017 (vacuum) with FCC Part 15B SDoC; most $49-69 clones show no listing on the page. ASSUMED requirement; supplier must prove with certificate numbers in the Intertek/UL directory.
Noise: target <=60 dB(A) at 1 m on max (leaders claim 50-60 dB; KTLA found oneisall loudest at max). To be measured on the sample.
Dust cup: 2.5 L vs oneisall LM2 1.5 L and Neakasa P1 Pro 1.0 L (small canister is a named complaint); full-cup window or indicator (Neakasa lacks one).
Filter: washable sponge + HEPA cartridge with 2 spare sets in the box.
Clipper: corded-through-vacuum or replaceable-battery clipper with ceramic moving blade and 2 spare blade sets in the box (clipper failure and hair pulling are recurring complaints).
Warranty: 2 years (Afloia and Neakasa already offer 2 years on Amazon; oneisall 1 year), funded by a written supplier defect-replacement term.
hero_spec.certifications_needed: UL 1017 (vacuum cleaners) via any NRTL (ETL/UL/CSA); clipper UL 859 if separately powered; FCC Part 15B for motor electronics; UN38.3 + UL 2054/62133 if a lithium battery clipper is included. Amazon requires ETL/UL for most plug-in products (third-party guides); not legally required for a DTC store but expected by insurers and needed to make a "safety-listed" claim.

certification.requirement: Not federally mandated for a DTC sale, but Amazon and big-box retailers require ETL/UL for most plug-in products (epicsourcing.co, compliancegate.com); product liability insurers and the "premium" rule make it effectively required. FCC Part 15B SDoC for motor electronics. Lithium-battery clippers: Amazon tightened third-party verification for rechargeable grooming devices (beBOLD, Aug 30 2026 deadline).
certification.cost_if_supplier_lacks: ETL $1,500-8,000; UL $2,000-10,000; FCC $1,000-4,000 per model; 4-8 weeks (epicsourcing.co 2026 guide). ESTIMATED
certification.suppliers_claiming_it: Jiangsu Schwarzwald Tech (hslair.en.alibaba.com) shows ETL certificate numbers 5013839 / 24-0244104 on its profile (product scope not verified); Zhejiang Beijing Technology (beijingkj.en.alibaba.com) lists ETL, CE, CB reports for pet electric products; a 120V/230V DC240 kit seller claims it "can pass CB, CE, ETL". No supplier found with UL or ETL proven specifically on a grooming vacuum. Houseclean Electric (Suzhou) lists FCC/CE/CB but not ETL. UNVERIFIED claims.
certification.leaders: Neither oneisall, Neakasa, FurMe nor Prepaw pages state a UL/ETL listing (checked product pages/snippets); UNKNOWN whether they hold one

landed.notes: Cash problem: one kit lands at roughly $78 (base: $48 FOB + $8 freight + $22 duty/cert) before fulfillment. A 50-unit MOQ is ~$3,900 and 200 units ~$15,600, against $300 supplier working capital and $1,800 total. Even 20 units (~$1,560 plus sample and cert) consumes nearly the whole budget. Storage fees at MCF/3PL excluded.

fit.customer: Owner of a medium-to-large double-coated or heavy-shedding dog (doodle, golden, husky, shepherd, lab) in a US house or apartment, 28-55, who pays a groomer $70-170 per visit and is tired of hair on floors and furniture; buys after a shedding-season peak or a skipped groomer appointment; values quiet operation because the dog fears vacuums.
fit.positioning: Against oneisall ($84.99, 1.5 L, 1-year): a safety-listed (ETL), measured-quiet kit with a 2.5 L cup, spare blades and filters in the box and a 2-year warranty - the "last grooming vacuum you buy" - priced above Amazon. Honest problem: the extra we can add (listing, spares, case, warranty) costs more than the $119 proven price supports.
fit.software_edge: Breed-based grooming schedule and attachment picker (quiz), blade/filter replacement reminders tied to order date (6-12 month blade interval), warranty registration and defect-claim flow, and order forwarding/delay notices for the 3PL/MCF.
fit.reorder: Real but small: oneisall replacement blade sells 700+/mo and generic blades 200-400/mo, filters 50-100+/mo, against ~11,000+/mo oneisall vacuum sales. Blade $12.99, filter set $12.99-19.99, recommended blade replacement every 6-12 months. A subscription would be ~1-2 orders per customer per year at ~$13-25.
fit.seasonality: Google "dog grooming vacuum" peaks Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 at 5,400 vs 4,400 baseline; spring shedding peak (SaleHoo says April high, October low). A January test lands in a seasonal high. Amazon data is from Q4 (gifting inflates).
risks: Economics fail at the proven price: base pre-ad $4.63 at $119 because landed cost (~$78) plus 13 lb billable fulfillment (~$19) eats the price
Cash: MOQ inventory buy ($1,560 for 20 units to $15,600 for 200) breaks the $1,800 budget and the $300 working capital line; no US-warehouse white-label dropshipper found
Tariff: 37.5% on 8508.11 from China (or 16.5% if classed as a clipper kit) - unresolved classification
Safety listing: no supplier proven to hold ETL/UL on a grooming vacuum; testing $1,500-8,000 and 4-8 weeks
Motorized product: defect/return risk (clipper and motor failures are the main complaint theme) on a 10 lb item that is costly to ship back
Competition: oneisall ~39% share with 14K reviews at $84.99 and clones at $49.99-69.99; DTC players (FurMe, Uproot, Prepaw) already run long-lived ads
Design patents on several Chinese pet-vacuum bodies (USD1,046,319; USD1,085,575; USD1,063,265): factory mold must be checked

proposed_pts.demand_note: 29,300+ units/mo floor across 87 page-1 grooming-vacuum listings, 11,800+ at $80-130, DTC brands at $160-200; but only ~200/mo on Amazon above $130.
proposed_pts.supplier_note: Dozens of factories at $30-60 FOB, but no US-warehouse white-label dropship found, MOQs 20-500, and no ETL/UL proven on a grooming vacuum.
proposed_pts.differentiation_note: Measurable upgrades exist (ETL, 2.5 L cup, dB, spares, 2-year warranty) but competitors already claim 50-60 dB, 2 L+ cups and 2-year warranties.
proposed_pts.risk_note: Mains appliance safety listing, 37.5% tariff, motor defects/returns on a 10 lb item, design patents on molds.
proposed_pts.ad_note: Excellent visual demo (hair sucked away mid-clip) for UGC; oneisall and Prepaw ads live 390-521 days; but $1.3-1.8 CPC and crowded feed.

verdict.reason: Proven demand at $65-110, but our landed plus fulfillment cost is ~$100 per kit, so the $119 proven-band price leaves $4.63 pre-ad (target CAC $3.47 vs $38.51). It only passes at ~$179, outside the Amazon-proven band, and needs an inventory buy several times the whole $1,800 budget.
top_unknowns: A US-warehouse white-label supplier (blind dropship, 1-unit orders) with a delivered price under ~$60 including shipping: would remove the inventory buy and could flip the economics
Tariff classification (8508.11 at 37.5% vs 8510.20 at 16.5%) - needs a customs broker or CBP ruling
Whether a new store can sell a $169-179 kit at <=$43 CPA (FurMe and Uproot prove the price exists DTC, but with established brands and review bases)
